rule_rows.note: Implements the matrix CLTV check for loans of $1,500,000 or less. Higher loan-amount tiers return unknown, so the full matrix job is not implemented.
Implements the $2,000,001–$3,000,000 matrix tier by applying its FICO and purpose-specific CLTV caps. It does not handle the other loan-amount tiers covered by job 105.

The rule enforces the $1.5MM delayed-financing cap, but does not check the required evidence of the prior all-cash acquisition. Its interest-only, low-loan-amount CLTV, and over-$2MM DSCR checks are not stated by the listed jobs.
The rule checks for Form 1007 on a vacant-property purchase, but job 76 also allows Form 1025 where applicable.
Repeats the short-term-rental caps and minimum FICO check in job 81.

Implements the listed minimum-DSCR checks and compares the ratio with the highest applicable threshold. It does not evaluate the above-80% LTV trigger, and it omits the additional approval conditions in jobs 10 and 6.

The rule applies the ITIN caps in job 58. For permanent and non-permanent residents, it flags the required identity or residency evidence as unavailable rather than verifying that the evidence is provided, so those checks are partial.
The rule checks whether tradelines meet a requirement; none of the listed jobs specifies this check.
The rule checks that the loan is for a business purpose and the property is an investment property. None of the listed jobs checks this eligibility requirement.
The rule checks that entity-borrower loans are for business purposes and investment properties. No listed job states that check.

Checks listed allowed entity types, document completeness, and that the first-time-homebuyer flag is false. It does not check the US-formed/based or foreign-ownership restrictions, guarantor-specific prior ownership and attestation requirements, or the full documentation conditions.

The clause covers the operating agreement, ownership evidence, name matching, and good-standing documentation. It does not state all details of jobs 30 and 33, such as the no-conflict condition and good-standing timing or foreign qualification requirements.

The aggregate entity-document completeness check covers the listed EIN, consent/resolution and POA requirements, and the foreign-qualification portion of job 33. The excerpt does not state job 33’s good-standing requirement.
Implements the printed housing-history CLTV caps by loan purpose and tier, but does not record that the tier definitions are pending Acra confirmation.

Implements the listed property eligibility and cap checks, short-sale seasoning caps, and escrow-waiver eligibility in part. It also takes the minimum of the caps it evaluates and checks CLTV, but does not cover every cap or separate impound requirement described by those jobs.
Implements parts of the vacant rate-and-term, vacant cash-out, rural-property, and above-80% LTV property-eligibility checks. Other conditions in those jobs are not implemented or are left unknown.
Checks only the six-month listed-for-sale trigger, which is part of job 9; it does not check the §11.5 loan conditions.
Checks the CLTV ≤ 70% threshold, but does not flag the LTV/CLTV basis mismatch described in the job.

The rule enforces the minimum loan amount and FICO floor for 5 Yr / 30 products (part of job 115) and the full stated parameters for 10 Yr / 40 loans (job 116). It does not apply job 115’s stated $3M maximum to the 5 Yr / 30 products. The first-time-homebuyer, vacant-property-refinance, and for-sale restrictions have no matching candidate job.
Checks the state-specific prepayment-penalty restrictions and their listed conditions.
Implements the matrix CLTV check in job 105 and applies the small-loan cap, but does not determine the overall governing cap across all applicable limits as job 111 requires.
Checks the 700 minimum FICO for an escrow waiver, one feature-specific floor in job 112.
Checks the $1.5MM delayed-financing cap, but not the prior all-cash acquisition evidence requirement.
The rule checks a 600 FICO floor for loans of $1,500,000 or less. None of the listed jobs states that check; the decisioning-score job concerns score selection, not a minimum score.

Validates the loan amount range and $50 increments (job 102), and applies tiered minimum-FICO checks (partial job 106). It does not route below-floor scores for Acra confirmation, and its middle tier does not distinguish purchase from refinance.
Checks the $1.5MM delayed-financing cap, but not evidence of the prior all-cash acquisition.

rule_rows.note: Checks the FICO/purpose matrix cap for the specific case of FICO 720 and cash-out (CLTV ≤ 55%). It does not implement the broader tier mapping or combine all governing caps.
The rule rejects short-term rentals but does not check nightly rentals or how rental income is used in the DSCR.
The rule calculates gross rental income divided by PITIA and applies the channel-specific minimum; jobs 58 and 86 state the same minimum-ratio check.
Checks that a current lease is in place for cash-out refinance, but not that it is unexpired and matches the subject property.
The rule rejects first-time-homebuyer applicants, matching the BOR-FTHB check and its cross-reference duplicate.
The rule requires entity borrowers to be labeled SPE and rejects series LLCs, but it does not check that the entity has only residential investment or rental properties and operates in that business.

The rule checks an allowed-type list, which also excludes prohibited types and series LLCs by omission, and checks that the first-time-homebuyer flag is false. It does not verify US formation/basis or foreign ownership, ownership nesting, single-purpose property qualifications, prior homeownership, or the required entity documents. The first-time-homebuyer check is only part of jobs 72 and 25.

The rule checks completeness of the listed entity-document package, covering operating agreements/bylaws, ownership evidence, name matching, and Good Standing documentation. It does not establish all details or timing requirements described by each job.
The entity-document completeness check covers the authorization/Power of Attorney requirements and the EIN documentation or exception request.
Checks that the applicant is not a first-time homebuyer, matching CRD-FTHB-XREF.

Implements the eligible and ineligible property-type checks in jobs 6 and 2. It also routes unrecognized property types to unknown, partially matching job 8. The additional 75% CLTV limit is not stated in these jobs.

Fully checks the expressly ineligible and eligible property types (jobs 2 and 6). Unknown property types and the Warrantable Condo/Two-Unit 75% CLTV cap cover parts of jobs 8 and 105, respectively; the rule does not implement their full checks.
Checks the CLTV-at-or-below-70% exemption threshold.
Implements the 6-month CLTV reserve check and the 24-month listed-property check. It does not implement the other reserve triggers or resolve overlapping triggers.
The rule checks the interest-only CLTV cap and sale-listing restriction; none of the listed jobs states either check.
Checks whether the six-month listed-for-sale condition applies, but returns unknown rather than verifying the required penalty term or state exception.
Checks the listed-for-sale 65% CLTV cap, which is one component of job 105’s governing-maximum calculation.
The rule excludes property_state SD, and no candidate job checks ineligible locations.
Checks the $1,500,000 delayed-financing cap, duplicating job 77.

The rule applies the Correspondent 700–719 FICO 60% CLTV cap, matching job 76 and implementing the cap portion of job 44. It does not check job 44’s 700 minimum score. The delayed-financing $1.5MM cap has no matching listed job.
Implements the CLTV-based reserve trigger: loans above 75% CLTV require at least 6 months of reserves. It does not aggregate the other reserve triggers in job 17.
Handles the escrow-waiver request and identifies Section 35 status as a required input, but does not check the loan-amount cap or mortgage-payment history.
The rule checks the loan amount range and $50 increments; none of the listed jobs checks loan amount.
The rule checks that occupancy is Non-Owner Occupied, matching job 89.

Checks eligible loan purposes and requires a current lease for Cash-Out Refinance, but does not match a supporting transaction document. The vacancy and DSCR/channel thresholds do not match any listed job.
The rule checks loan amount limits and increments, plus a conditional CLTV cap. None of the listed jobs states these checks.

Implements job 78's FICO/purpose matrix cap. It also partially implements job 105 by checking the matrix cap and loan amount, but does not combine the other listed caps or apply the declining-market reduction.
